reference.source: Textbook of Pediatric Rheumatology / ILAR & PRINTO criteria
clinicalPearls: Falls within the juvenile spondyloarthritis spectrum and typically affects older boys, often with a family history of HLA-B27-associated disease
Enthesitis, inflammation at the insertion of tendons and ligaments into bone, is characteristic and commonly affects the Achilles tendon, plantar fascia and around the knee
Peripheral arthritis is usually asymmetrical and predominantly affects the lower limbs, including hips
Axial and sacroiliac involvement may develop over time, producing inflammatory back pain with morning stiffness that improves with activity
Acute symptomatic anterior uveitis (a painful, red, photophobic eye) is typical, in contrast to the chronic silent uveitis of oligoarticular disease
Strong association with HLA-B27, and overlap with reactive arthritis and inflammatory bowel disease-related arthropathy
Management uses NSAIDs, intra-articular corticosteroids and, for persistent or axial disease, TNF inhibition
reference.pathophysiology: Enthesitis-related arthritis is a juvenile spondyloarthropathy in which inflammation centres on the enthesis, the site where tendons, ligaments and joint capsules insert into bone. In genetically predisposed children, particularly those carrying HLA-B27, aberrant innate and adaptive immune responses, with a prominent role for the interleukin-23/interleukin-17 axis, drive entheseal and synovial inflammation and, in some, sacroiliitis and spinal involvement. Chronic inflammation can lead to new bone formation, ankylosis and progressive axial disease resembling ankylosing spondylitis in adulthood.
additionalDifferentials: Mechanical or overuse enthesopathy and apophysitis (e.g. Osgood-Schlatter, Sever disease)
Reactive arthritis following gastrointestinal or genitourinary infection
additionalInvestigations: HLA-B27 typing to support the diagnosis
Inflammatory markers (erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein)
MRI of the sacroiliac joints to detect early sacroiliitis before radiographic change
Ultrasound of entheses to confirm active enthesitis
Ophthalmology assessment for symptomatic anterior uveitis
Screening for inflammatory bowel disease when gastrointestinal symptoms are present
Radiographs of affected joints and sacroiliac joints in established disease
redFlags: Progressive inflammatory back pain with restricted spinal mobility indicating axial disease
Acute painful red eye requiring urgent ophthalmology review
Fever and systemic upset suggesting infection
Weight loss, bloody diarrhoea or anaemia suggesting inflammatory bowel disease
reference.prognosis: The course is variable; some children have limited peripheral disease, while others progress to axial spondyloarthritis with sacroiliitis and reduced spinal mobility in adulthood. Early recognition and TNF inhibition can improve symptom control and may modify axial progression.
pitfalls: Dismissing entheseal heel and knee pain as mechanical growing pains
Overlooking early sacroiliitis because plain radiographs are insensitive early on
Assuming HLA-B27 negativity excludes the diagnosis
Failing to warn families about symptomatic acute uveitis
references: ILAR classification of juvenile idiopathic arthritis
management: NSAIDs as first-line treatment for enthesitis, peripheral arthritis and inflammatory back pain
Physiotherapy and a regular exercise programme to maintain spinal and joint mobility and function
Local corticosteroid injections for persistent enthesitis or an isolated inflamed peripheral joint
Conventional disease-modifying agents such as sulfasalazine or methotrexate for peripheral arthritis, recognising these do not control axial disease
Escalate to TNF inhibitors, or IL-17 inhibitors, for axial disease or peripheral and entheseal disease refractory to first-line therapy
Urgent ophthalmology referral and topical corticosteroids for acute symptomatic anterior uveitis
Monitor growth, disease activity and the sacroiliac joints with MRI, and screen for associated inflammatory bowel disease
Paediatric rheumatology multidisciplinary care with planned transition to adult services
